findings.title: Atomic report write leaks temp files on failure
findings.description: `NamedTemporaryFile(delete=False)` is created, then `handle.write` or `temp.replace(target)` can raise `OSError`. The `except OSError` branch logs and re-raises but never unlinks the temp file. Each failed write, such as disk full, leaves a hidden `.{name}.XXXX` file in the runs dir. The batch writes after every item and item resume rewrites too, so repeated failures can pile these up. The existing tests check only that the old report survives, not that no temp file is left behind. Remove the temp file in the failure path, and add an assertion for it.

findings.title: `run_item` imports private functions from `run.py` through a circular import
findings.description: `handle_item_resume` does a function-local import of `_apply_param_overrides` and `_run_pipeline_sdk` from `run.py`. The code comment says this is because `run.py` imports this module, and each import needs a `reportPrivateUsage` suppression. That is a layering cycle held together by suppressions. Moving the shared runner and param helpers into a neutral module, or passing `run_body` and the override parser in from `run.py`, would remove both the cycle and the suppressions.

findings.title: Blocking sync git, cf and file work inside async `resume_item`
findings.description: The async path calls `run_git`, `restore_target`, `dirty_paths`, `verify_git_state`, `cf_client.list_slices` and `list_tasks`, and `report.write` directly. All of these are subprocess or file I/O. The Python rules require sync code inside `async def` to be under 1 ms or moved to an executor. The impact is low today because the CLI runs a single task under `asyncio.run`. The rule still applies, and `_write_each_report` in the executor already uses `asyncio.to_thread` for the same write.

findings.title: `_pre_flag` silently defaults a missing flag kind
findings.description: `FlagKind(str(item.get(FLAG_KIND_KEY, FlagKind.NOT_READY)))` quietly labels any source-flagged item as `not_ready` when the source set no kind. The project rule forbids silent fallback values. A third-party or custom source that sets only `flag_reason` is therefore misclassified without any signal. The test `test_a_source_flag_without_a_kind_is_not_ready` locks this in. Either require the source to set the kind or log at WARNING when the default applies.

findings.title: `ItemRerun.replace` raises a bare `StopIteration` when the index is missing
findings.description: `next(i for i, r in enumerate(records) if r.index == record.index)` has no default. If the index is absent, `StopIteration` escapes. Inside the coroutine that becomes an opaque `RuntimeError`, and it fires from the `finally` handling in `_finish_each_report`, where it could mask the original fault. `_reconcile` has the same pattern. Raise an explicit error naming the index instead.

findings.title: Layering and style nits
findings.description:
- `StateManager.list_runs` now imports `batch_report` just to learn a filename suffix, which couples state storage to the report module. A shared constant in a lower-level module would be cleaner.
- `_write_each_report`'s signature in `executor.py` is about 103 characters, over the 88-character limit, and `executor.py` keeps growing well past the roughly 300-line guideline.
- `resume_item` ends with an unreachable `raise AssertionError` after its `with` block.
- The new tests lean heavily on `# type: ignore`, which sits poorly with the strict-pyright rule.

findings.title: Run lock, reserved params and report schema
findings.description:
- The `flock` is non-blocking, released when the descriptor closes, and keyed to the per-worktree git dir. Every failure path logs at ERROR and maps to exit 2, and tests cover it.
- Reserved control params are defined once in `control_params.py` and enforced at the CLI, the loader and item-resume params.
- `report.json` has versioned load errors, and the new behaviors have tests, including the halt and failed-write observability paths.
